features.title: Automatic feature branch creation tied to OpenSpec
features.description: When a spec change is detected (new version or x-spec-id in openapi.yaml), automatically create a git branch feature/<service>-<spec-id> before generating artifacts.
features.motivation: Isolate each spec iteration in its own branch, making it traceable from OpenSpec change to git history.

branchNaming.optionA: feature/<service>-spec-v<info.version> — derived from semver in openapi.yaml info block
branchNaming.optionB: feature/<service>-<x-spec-id> — derived from a custom x-spec-id extension field in openapi.yaml info block (preferred: more semantic)

implementation.specIdResolution: Read info.x-spec-id (or info.version fallback) from libs/<service>/specs/openapi.yaml
implementation.changeDetection: Compare openapi.yaml info.version against microservice.json specVersion field

features.title: Spec scope guard — prevent modifications outside service boundary
features.description: A new check:spec-scope command validates that all modified files (git diff --name-only HEAD) are within libs/<service>/ when working on a feature branch for that service.
features.motivation: Enforce the SDD contract: a spec change should only affect the files it declares it generates or modifies.

conditionallyAllowed: libs/shared/ — allowed if the service explicitly declares a shared dependency
forbidden: apps/api/src/app.module.ts (unless it is a new service registration)
design.triggerPoint: scripts/workflows/index.ts verify() — after existing validation gates

features.title: Production log shipping and transports
features.description: Track the production logging readiness checklist and evaluate production destinations for Pino logs after the deployment and observability platform is selected. The structured-logging change keeps production output as JSON on stdout and uses pino-pretty only in development.
features.motivation: Route operational logs to an appropriate collector or managed destination with deliberate retention, resilience, security, and cost controls instead of coupling the API to an unselected vendor.

considerations: Select the production collector and destination based on the deployment platform.
Use Pino transports in worker threads for log processing that could block the API event loop.
Define delivery failure, buffering, backpressure, retry, and shutdown behavior.
Preserve redaction before logs leave the process and define retention and volume limits.
Keep stdout JSON available for local operation and platform-native collection.

productionReadinessChecklist.item: Control levels with LOG_LEVEL; default to warn in production and info outside production.
Use pino-pretty only in development and raw JSON in production.
Limit external destinations to warn/error and configure production transports.
Review high-volume paths to avoid per-item logging in loops and sample noisy health checks where appropriate.
Never log request or response bodies.
Redact credentials, tokens, passwords, card numbers, security codes, and sensitive headers with serialized-output regression tests.
Serialize exceptions under err rather than logging err.message alone.
Use child loggers for API modules and requests; add job context when background jobs are introduced.
Set service and environment base fields; add build/version metadata from APP_VERSION and GIT_SHA with a dev fallback.
Configure multiple production destinations such as file and external monitoring only after deployment requirements are known.
Keep logger configuration in a dedicated host configuration file registered once by AppModule.

features.title: Expose API documentation in production behind auth
features.description: Enable GET /docs and GET /docs/openapi.json in production behind session authentication, building on the dev-only API docs capability (add-platform-api-docs) that already provides the API_DOCS_ENABLED flag.
features.motivation: The merged OpenAPI reference is currently a development-only tool; enabling it in production would let consumers and integrators consult the authoritative contracts of the running API, but the merged document is internal information that must not be public, so exposure requires an authenticated audience.

considerations: Flip or extend API_DOCS_ENABLED rather than adding a new mechanism; the production default stays off until this feature lands.
Decide the audience: any authenticated session versus an admin role, and whether apps/web may link to the reference for signed-in users.
Reuse the existing middleware patterns (SessionValidationMiddleware scoping and origin validation) instead of a bespoke auth path.
Self-host the Scalar UI bundle instead of loading it from the public CDN, and pin the version for determinism.
Define caching headers for the spec JSON (private, no-store or short max-age) since the document changes with each release.
Consider disabling the interactive request console in production to avoid sending credentials through the reference UI.

features.title: Make local Playwright runs use an isolated Vite server
features.description: Prevent local browser E2E runs from silently reusing an unrelated or stale Vite server already listening on the configured port.
features.motivation: A reused stale app can make the suite test code that is not the current workspace and produce misleading results, while CI already starts a fresh server.

design.defaultBehavior: Start a fresh Vite server with strictPort for local and CI E2E runs.
design.optionalReuse: If reuse is retained for faster local iteration, make it an explicit opt-in and verify the server belongs to this workspace/build before reuse.
considerations: Keep the dedicated E2E port independent of the normal web development port.
Ensure a port conflict fails clearly instead of falling back to or accepting an unknown server.
Document any opt-in reuse mode and its limitations.

features.title: Stronger password policy and breached-password blocking
features.description: Harden the account password policy beyond the current 8–128 character length rule and refuse passwords known to be breached. Consider a higher minimum length and optional character-class or passphrase guidance, and integrate a breach check such as the Better Auth haveibeenpwned plugin or the Pwned Passwords k-anonymity range API.
features.motivation: The current policy only enforces 8–128 characters with no complexity or breach screening, so users can set weak or already-compromised passwords that are accepted at activation, login, and password reset.

currentState: Enforced in the web form (minLength), the Zod controller schemas, PasswordValueObject (MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH / MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH), and Better Auth (minPasswordLength 8 / maxPasswordLength 128 defaults).
No uppercase, number, or symbol requirement and no breached-password check (haveibeenpwned plugin not configured).
goals: Define one password policy shared by activation, password reset, and any future credential change.
Reject passwords found in known breach corpora without sending the full password.
Keep user-facing messages actionable and non-disclosing.

strength: Raise the minimum length (for example 12) and document the choice.
Optionally require character classes or encourage passphrases, weighing usability against security.
Expose the policy to the web so the form can validate before submit.
breachBlocking: Enable the Better Auth haveibeenpwned plugin if the installed 1.7.7 version supports it.
Alternatively query the Pwned Passwords range API with SHA-1 k-anonymity (send only the hash prefix).
Decide fail-open versus fail-closed behavior when the breach service is unreachable, with timeouts and caching.

considerations: Apply the same policy at activation (POST /auth/signup/complete) and password reset (POST /auth/reset-password/confirm).
Reuse the central password hashing/verification path so a policy change cannot be bypassed.
Validate before consuming a registration token so a rejected password does not consume the link.
Add startup-validated config (for example AUTH_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH) with safe defaults.
Update PasswordValueObject, the Better Auth emailAndPassword config, controller Zod schemas, the web forms, OpenAPI descriptions, and .env.example.
Add tests for the length boundary, character-class rules, a breached-password rejection, and breach-service failure behavior.
Document the chosen policy and its trade-offs.

features.title: Migrate build/test orchestration to Nx targets with remote cache
features.description: Turn the pnpm-script orchestration (root package.json scripts plus scripts/cli.ts) into executable Nx targets per project (nx build api, nx test users, ...) so Nx can cache task outputs and run affected-only work in CI.
features.motivation: Nx is currently used as a project map (project graph, tags, module boundaries) but not as an executor: project.json files define no targets, so targetDefaults in nx.json are inert and nx affected has nothing to affect. At the current repo size this is fine and CI runs the pnpm scripts directly; once the suite or the project count grows, per-project targets unlock affected-only pipelines and local/remote caching.

currentState: All tasks run through root package.json scripts and scripts/cli.ts; no project.json defines executable targets.
nx.json defaultBase was aligned to develop when the GitHub Actions CI change landed.
CI (ci.yml) runs pnpm scripts in single jobs; no per-target caching.
considerations: Add build/test/lint targets to each project.json, backed by the existing scripts rather than duplicating them.
Keep scripts/cli.ts orchestration alongside Nx targets during the migration; avoid a big-bang cutover.
Enable a shared cache (self-hosted or Nx Cloud) consumed by CI so PR runs reuse main-branch artifacts.
Switch PR pipelines to nx affected --base develop once targets exist, replacing the always-run job set.

features.title: First production deployment and platform smoke tests
features.description: Execute the production deploy path documented in docs/deployment.md on nan.builders Spaces: bootstrap the three service databases, create the API and web apps, and run the first-deploy smoke tests. The deploy-path change (add-production-deploy-path) ships the images, the self-migrating entrypoint, and the runbook; this feature is the operational first run that verifies the platform assumptions the change left open.
features.motivation: The production deploy path is complete as code and verified locally (scripts/smoke-production-images.mjs covers the container scenarios against the compose Postgres), but the platform-specific behavior — cross-app DNS visibility, migrate deploy in deploy logs, public HTTPS health, same-site session cookies, and version/commit fields in platform logs — can only be observed on a live deployment. Tracking it here keeps the first deployment of every project derived from this boilerplate an explicit, repeatable checklist instead of tribal knowledge.

smokeTests: Bootstrap auth_db, users_db, and orders_db on the managed PostgreSQL instance and rotate any database credential that was ever shared in plaintext.

Deploy the API app (docker/api/Dockerfile, internal port 3000, runtime env from the production section of .env.example including APP_VERSION and GIT_SHA): deploy logs must show prisma migrate deploy applying the auth and users migrations, then the listening log.
GET https://<api-app-origin>/users/health returns 200 with {"status":"ok"} from the public URL, which also proves cross-app DNS visibility.

Deploy the web app (docker/web/Dockerfile, internal port 80, build variable VITE_API_URL=<api origin>): a deep link renders the client and a sign-in round trip completes with the session cookie preserved (same-site flow, no SameSite=None changes).
With APP_VERSION and GIT_SHA set, an operational log entry on the platform's log view carries matching version and commit fields.

updatedPipeline: openapi.yaml edited with new version or x-spec-id
pnpm propose → detect spec change → git checkout -b feature/<service>-<spec-id> → generateFromSpec()
pnpm commit_flow → guard: assert current branch matches feature/* pattern

openQuestions: Use x-spec-id extension field in openapi.yaml (optionB) or derive branch name from semver (optionA)?
Should libs/shared/ changes be allowed within a spec scope without explicit declaration?
Should commit_flow hard-fail if not on a feature/* branch, or just warn?
